entries.name: GOOGLE_DRIVE_ROOT_FOLDER_ID
entries.description: The Drive folder the business shares with Brain A. Everything below it is read as metadata (names, types, folders, sizes, edit times); file contents are never downloaded.
howToGet: Open the folder in Google Drive and copy the id after /folders/ in the address bar.
The Google account that connects must be able to open the folder. A whole shared drive can be read instead, or as well, with GOOGLE_DRIVE_SHARED_DRIVE_IDS.

entries.name: GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_REFRESH_TOKEN
entries.description: The refresh token from connecting the business's Google account with the three read-only scopes drive.metadata.readonly, spreadsheets.readonly and calendar.events.readonly. It uses the same OAuth client as Gmail but is a separate connection, because each connector stops if its token holds any scope beyond its own. Google doesn't rotate it; the instance keeps a sealed copy in case Google ever returns a new one.
howToGet: Have the account owner connect to the instance's OAuth client with access_type=offline, prompt=consent and exactly these scopes: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.metadata.readonly, https://www.googleapis.com/auth/spreadsheets.readonly and https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.events.readonly (spreadsheets.readonly only if GOOGLE_SHEETS_RANGES is set, calendar.events.readonly only if calendars are read). Google's OAuth 2.0 Playground with the client's own credentials works (add https://developers.google.com/oauthplayground as an authorized redirect URI).

The connector stops if the token holds anything else, such as drive.readonly (which can download files), drive, drive.file, spreadsheets, calendar, calendar.readonly, calendar.events or a Gmail scope, so don't add them.
Copy the refresh token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: GOOGLE_DRIVE_SHARED_DRIVE_IDS
entries.description: Shared drives to read whole, besides the shared folder: comma-separated shared drive ids. Each is walked like a folder and gets its own change feed.
howToGet: Leave empty to read only the shared folder.
Open the shared drive in Google Drive and copy the id after /folders/ in the address bar.

entries.name: GOOGLE_DRIVE_FILE_NAMES
entries.description: Whether file and folder names are kept: keep (the default) or drop, for a business whose files are named after customers. With drop, only ids, types, folders, sizes and times are kept.
howToGet: Leave empty for keep. Use drop if file names carry customers' names.

entries.name: GOOGLE_SHEETS_RANGES
entries.description: The only spreadsheet ranges whose values are read: comma-separated spreadsheetId/Sheet!A1:F500 entries. Sheet names may hold letters, digits, spaces, _ . and -, quoted when they hold a space. Nothing else is read from any spreadsheet. List ranges without customers' personal details; a cell that is only an email address is kept as a correspondent reference.
howToGet: Leave empty to read no spreadsheet values.
Open the spreadsheet and copy the id between /d/ and /edit in the address bar, then add / and the range in A1 notation, as Google Sheets shows it.

entries.name: GOOGLE_CALENDAR_IDS
entries.description: Which calendars' appointments are read: primary (the default, the connected account's own calendar), none, or comma-separated calendar ids such as a shared appointments calendar's address. Not a secret, but it names the calendars.
howToGet: Leave empty for primary. Use none to read no calendars.
For another calendar, open its settings in Google Calendar and copy the Calendar ID under Integrate calendar.

entries.name: GOOGLE_PUSH_CHANNEL_TOKEN
entries.description: The token Drive and Calendar push channels are opened with and echo back in X-Goog-Channel-Token, which is how the instance tells a genuine notification from a forged one (Google doesn't sign them). Only used once push channels are turned on through the write gate.
howToGet: Generated automatically by npm run secrets:setup.
After rotating it, open new push channels: notifications on the old ones are refused.
